name: Namaz Akışı: Prayer Times
subtitle: Free, ad-free adhan times
promotionalText: Reminds you so you don't miss prayer time, and grows more insistent as the time runs short. Free, ad-free, offline and in 78 languages. Your data stays on your phone.
description:
When the day is a rush, it is easy to miss that a prayer time has begun, or to hear the adhan, think “I'll pray in a minute” and forget. It happens to most of us. Namaz Akışı was made for these moments. It tells you when a prayer time begins, calls you more insistently as the time runs short, and helps you fit prayer into your day. It is free, ad-free and works without the internet.

IF YOU'VE GROWN USED TO NOTIFICATIONS
A single notification is easy to swipe away. Prayer Guardian sets 1 to 6 reminders for each prayer time. As the time runs short, the reminders come more often and their tone grows firmer. On iOS 26 and later, the reminder you choose rings as a real alarm, even when your phone is on silent. Pick the reminder sound from the app's sounds or add your own sound file. Once you say “I've prayed”, the reminders for that prayer go quiet.

IF YOUR DAY IS BUSY
If a meeting in your calendar falls at the end of a prayer time, the app reminds you to pray before the meeting. For Jumu'ah and the prayers you want to pray at the mosque, it lets you know as early as your walk there takes. If you haven't prayed Isha, it reminds you before your bedtime.

SEE IT WITHOUT UNLOCKING
The time left until the next prayer stays on your Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. Prayer times appear in Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets. Mark “I've prayed” from Control Center or with Siri, without opening the app.

NO RINGING PHONE AT THE MOSQUE
The Prayer Focus, which you set up once with the app's guide, silences your iPhone when you arrive at a mosque you've added and restores it when you leave.

ON THE ROAD AND ABROAD
Prayer times are calculated from your coordinates, following the timetable the mosques of that country use. In Türkiye, the Diyanet method is used. Abroad, the app suggests the local timetable, and the method never changes without your approval. You find the Qibla with the compass or the camera view. None of this needs the internet.

IF YOUR QADA DEBT FEELS DAUNTING
A wizard calculates your qada debt. After each obligatory prayer, the app suggests one qada, which you deduct from your Qada log with one tap. If you like, missed obligatory prayers are added to the log automatically when the prayer day ends.

IF BUILDING A ROUTINE IS HARD
Every day you pray in full adds one day to your streak. If a long streak breaks, two full days win it back, so one off day doesn't wipe out your effort. The Progress tab shows a daily, weekly and monthly breakdown. If you like, the app also reminds you of Tahajjud, Duha and Awwabin times.

START THE DAY WITH A VERSE
A verse with its translation, renewed at every Fajr, sits in a widget on your Home Screen and Lock Screen. With Shortcuts, it can become your Lock Screen wallpaper every morning, with the background, font and ornament you choose, or your own photo.

IN YOUR OWN LANGUAGE
The app is available in 78 languages. Screens and notifications work in the language you choose. In languages such as Arabic, Urdu and Persian, the interface runs from right to left.

WATCH, TABLET AND TV
• On Apple Watch, you see the time left, say “I've prayed” from your wrist, find the Qibla and do your tasbih. Your watch reminds you when your phone is out of reach. The Fajr alarm vibrates only your wrist, without ringing the phone or waking the person beside you.
• On iPad, the wider screen shows the whole day at a glance. Your phone and tablet pass your “I've prayed” to each other over your home network.
• Send your location to the TV at home with a QR code, and see prayer times on the big screen.

YOUR DATA STAYS WITH YOU
You don't need an account. The app has no ads, tracking or analytics. Your location is used only to calculate prayer times and the Qibla, and it never reaches us.

OPEN SOURCE
I develop Namaz Akışı with the intention of sadaqah jariyah. The app is free, and its source code is open to everyone under the GNU GPLv3 license:
https://github.com/furkanisikay/namazakisi
whatsNew:
- The app is now available in 78 languages; choose yours in Settings. Languages such as Arabic, Urdu and Persian are shown from right to left.
- Accurate prayer times anywhere in the world: a calculation method for your country, and cities worldwide.
- Verse of the day: a new verse with its translation every day, in a Home Screen and Lock Screen widget. With Shortcuts, you can also make it your Lock Screen wallpaper.
- Choose the reminder sound from the app's sounds or add your own sound file.
- Security and stability improvements.
